title: [LoRA] Update LoRA expand kernel heuristic (#32425)

image.wheel_note: first PyPI release after merge (2026-01-20 > 2026-01-16); picked by gen_tasks.py from PyPI upload dates.

workload.note: lora_expand custom op via LoRAKernelMeta (as tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py): 3 slices x hidden 1024 (QKV-like), rank 16, 1 LoRA, 16 and 256 tokens, plus a 1-slice x 4096 control; PR = default block_n 128 -> max(64, next_pow2(128//num_slices)) (untuned GPU path). CUDA-event us per call. Author: _lora_expand_kernel ~14 -> ~10 us (profiler), e2e +1%.

policy.one_run_is: one `docker run` of the workload cmd per arm per repeat (same image, arm tree swapped in by the prelude)

contention_gate.rules: wait while another tenant uses the GPU (>5 % util or a foreign compute process >1 GiB) or the CPU (load1 > nproc/2)

policy.machine_snapshot: machine.py snapshot per workload run -> data/pr_<n>/work/machine_<arm>_<i>.json

arm_isolation.tree: wipe the wheel's vllm/*.py, copy the arm's vllm/ over site-packages (compiled .so stay)
arm_isolation.files: overlay ONLY task.json:source_files from the arm over the wheel's own tree
arm_isolation.tests_benchmarks: copied from the PR's merge tree to /t without a sibling vllm/ package

policy.noise_model: measure.py: paired log-speedup, MAD sigma, theta = clip(k*sigma, theta_min, theta_max) with k/theta from config.yaml:measure

headline: lora_expand_3slice_h1024_t16

reported.experiments_note: reported = numbers from the PR body (author's machine)

author_hardware_args.text: * During profiling we found qkv_proj expand kernel takes more time than shrink kernel. We found it's because layers like `QKVParallelLinearWithLoRA` has num_slices > 1, N (output_size) is smaller in each slice. Therefore, we can set smaller
* Profiling shows `_lora_expand_kernel` improves about 30%. (With tuned config, it can achieve the 2x more performance gain.)
